lead: Real property a person can own — houses, flats, factory-built and floating homes, land and estates, unusual conversions and burial places — organised by property type, with architectural style and regional house tradition as cross-cutting views; commercial and industrial buildings are out, and garden buildings live in Home Fixtures.

b.w: Weighed first by every buying guide; a filter and map, never a department.

b.v: freehold > share of freehold > leasehold / condominium > co-operative
b.w: Determines what is actually owned; checked before survey in most jurisdictions.

b.v: roof, walls, damp, plumbing, wiring, heating (RICS Home Survey Levels 1–3)
b.w: Survey follows title.

b.v: EPC A (92+) > B > C > D > E > F > G
b.w: Running cost and comfort; stored only as a view, never for one home.
Last in the order.

depts.t: Dwellings built as houses, whether attached or free-standing, small or grand; one dwelling inside a larger building → Flats & apartments, a house converted from another building → Unusual & converted properties. depts.ax: Where does the house stand and how grand is it: in a town row, on a suburban or detached plot, in the countryside, or as a grand seat?
depts.note: Buyer property types first; architectural style and regional tradition are views over the same houses.

depts.msum: The ten largest US builders closed a record 44.7 % of new single-family homes in 2024, led by D.R. Horton (NAHB). In the UK, Vistry overtook Barratt as the largest builder in September 2024; Barratt then merged with Redrow in October 2024. 2024 completions: Vistry 17,225, Barratt 14,004 (year to June), Taylor Wimpey 10,593 and Persimmon 10,664; these are counts, not shares, and the reporting years differ.

ax: What is the property: a house, a unit in a larger building, a factory-built or floating home, land, a converted or odd building, or a burial space?
key: 1. Is it a house, from cottage to castle, standing alone or in a row? → Houses
2. Is it one dwelling, or a share of one, inside a larger building, or a whole building of flats? → Flats & apartments
3. Was it made in a factory, carried on a chassis, portable, or afloat? → Factory-built, mobile & floating homes
4. Is it land, a farm or estate building, a plot or a parking space? → Land & estates
5. Was the building first made for something other than a house, or built in an odd way (barn, mill, church, fort, folly, cave, tree)? → Unusual & converted properties
6. Is it a space to bury a body or keep ashes? → Burial places
Precedence: a mobile or floating home is step 3 before step 1; a whole converted building is step 5 but one converted flat is step 2; a farmhouse with its land is step 1, bare farmland step 4.
